text:
alex: Hey, canary looks slower this morning — heatmap and sparklines are ~3-5s slower on initial load.

jia: yup seeing on EU canary, perf dashboard shows spike around 1715839200.

tara: network waterfall shows duplicate requests for client-main.js: two GETs back-to-back, second is 200 (network), first is 200 (disk cache). parse time skyrockets.

sahil: we rolled out routing policy change last night (region-shard + sticky). could that cause service worker scope mismatch? :thinking:

jia: possible. here's the snippet from the devtools log:
```
GET /static/client-main.js 200 (disk cache)  → 0ms
GET /static/client-main.js 200 (network)    → 180ms
Parse & Compile: +220ms
```

ryan: deploy-bot shows canary deploy at 1715835600 by ryan. same time as routing change.

deploy-bot: canary deploy completed — redispatch-policy=v2 enabled

alex: also seeing repeated bundle bytes size jump (gzipped ~120KB→210KB) for some sessions.

tara: that smells like server-side bundle variant selection — different backend is returning non-optimized bundle when cache miss happens.

sahil: idea: routing change routes some requests to an older fleet that doesn't have the optimized gzipped bundle in its CDN origin/local cache -> K/V cache miss + fallback to full payload.

jia: corroborating — telemetry traces show backend latency correlated with duplicate bundle fetches and kvcache.miss tag.

ryan: quick mitigation options:
- roll back routing change for canary
- disable service worker for canary (force single network fetch)
- push origin prune to ensure all backends have latest bundle

alex: I'd prefer rollback to minimize user impact. we'll also add a telemetry counter for duplicate bundle requests and an alert when JS parse > 150ms on first-load.

tara: i'll open a sweep issue to verify service worker scope & cache key generation across regions.

sahil: i'll prepare the rollback and post ETA.

ryan: thanks — tagging infra-oncall @sahil for rollback.

sahil: rollback started, ETA ~8m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alex: sounded good. after rollback, can we run a canary with telemetry flag that forces bundle hash in headers so we can detect mismatches?

jia: yes, adding req header X-Bundle-Hash -> telemetry. i'll add to the canary pipeline.

ryan: once we stabilise, follow-up: audit CDN origin alignment and service-worker cache-key logic.

alex: great. created GH issue #7423 and linked telemetry dashboard.

tara: thanks, all. keep updates here.
